notes: Very common at the end of a sentence. It can soften a suggestion or request, ask for agreement, or add a guessing tone.
Most often the classifier for books and notebooks. It can also mean a copy or volume, and in other common words it can mean root or origin.
Most often marks comparison in the pattern A 比 B + adjective or phrase. It can also mean to compare.
Most often the negative command word don't. It also commonly means other in words like 别的 and 别人.
The basic negation word in Chinese. It usually comes before a verb or adjective.
Classifier for how many times something happens. It is very common with numbers.
Marks a starting point in time or place. It is very common in movement patterns and time expressions.
Placed after an adjective or phrase and before a verb to mark the way an action is done.
One of the most common grammar words in Chinese. It marks possession and links modifiers to nouns.
Placed before a number to show order, as in first, second, or third.
Common as an adjective meaning correct or right, and also as a preposition meaning to or toward.
Most often means a minute in time. It also commonly means a point in scores or grades.
The most common general classifier in Mandarin. It is used with many everyday nouns.
The core verb means give. It is also very common before a person to mean to or for.
Often means with in everyday speech. It can also mean to follow someone or something.
Very common adverb meaning still, also, or yet, depending on the sentence.
Very common in choice questions, where it means or. It can also mean still in other contexts.
Most often the conjunction and. It can also mean with in some common patterns.
Most often expresses ability or knowing how to do something. It is also a common noun meaning a meeting.
Often used as the classifier for rooms or spaces. It can also mean between, and in some words it means a room.

primary_gloss: then; right away; as soon as
notes: Common grammar word for quick sequence, early occurrence, or emphasis, as in as soon as or right away.
Most often means mouth. It can also mean an opening, and it is a common classifier for family members in some expressions.
Grammar particle that marks a completed action or a new situation.
Basic location word meaning inside or in. It often comes after a place word.
Sentence-final particle used to ask a yes-no question.
Common negator for past actions, completed actions, and not having something.
Used for not having something or for saying something does not exist.
Most often means door or gate. It is also a common classifier for school subjects, trades, or skills.
Plural suffix used mainly with pronouns and some words for people.
Sentence-final particle used in follow-up questions, topic continuation, or a softer ongoing tone.
Used as a polite marker in requests. It also commonly means to invite or to ask someone to do something.
Very common word meaning on or above, previous or last, and also to go up or get on.
Basic verb meaning to be.
Very common yes-no question pattern built from a verb and its negated form.
Common adverb for saying something is too much, or very in an exclamatory pattern.
Very common word meaning under or below, next, and also to go down or get off.
Used for doing one thing first before another.
Common adverb meaning also or too.

primary_gloss: a little bit; for a moment
notes: Common phrase that softens an action as brief, light, or quick.
Can mean one side, and it also appears in the pattern for doing two things at once.
Common verb meaning to have something or that something exists.
Usually means to do something again or one more time, often in future or repeated actions.

primary_gloss: be at; be in; be on
notes: Most often the location verb meaning to be at or in a place. It is also used before a place like at, in, or on.
Common location word meaning here or this side.
Common location word meaning here.
Common spoken form of here.
Shows that a state, action, or posture is continuing, as in open, wearing, or holding.
Most often an adverb meaning really. It can also mean real or true.
Commonly used as an adverb meaning really. It can also mean true or real.
Placed before a verb to show an action is in progress right now.
Often follows a noun to mean among, in, or within. The middle sense is also common in fixed expressions and compounds.
Common suffix in many everyday nouns, such as 杯子 and 桌子. It is often not translated directly.
